exposure: Fetal subcutaneous tissue (SCT) thickness (measured by ultrasound and calipers)
cohort: The study participants were 117 pregnant women (97 controls and 20 with GDM) scheduled for cesarean delivery at a gestational age of >=37 weeks.
finding: Fetal subcutaneous fat thickness measured shortly before delivery correlates with and can predict insulin resistance in neonates, particularly for those born to mothers with effectively managed GDM.
cross-section timing: Fetal SCT thickness was measured immediately before delivery and within 48 hours after delivery; cord blood analysis was performed immediately after delivery.
